owner.occupation: Youth football coach at a club academy (U13-U15)

world.bio: I coach the U13 to U15 groups at a club academy on the east side of São Paulo. I played as a midfielder in the lower divisions until a knee injury at 29, did my coaching licence at the CBF academy, and have been with the club for six years. I speak decent English from courses and years of watching coaching videos, and some Spanish. Every training plan I have ever written is in a battered green notebook I carry everywhere.
skills_assets: CBF B-licence coaching certificate, six years with the same academy
A stack of notebooks with training plans, about 400 sessions, sorted by theme: pressing triggers, build-up from the back, small-sided games
Video analysis with a cheap action camera and Hudl; I cut clips for the boys after each match
English good enough to run a session; Spanish for the Argentine coaches I trade ideas with
A reputation among parents for developing technically clean midfielders; two former players now in pro academies
The academy's pre-season and mid-season blocks are paid; from mid-December to late February he has no income from the club

projects.name: U14 season push
projects.text: We are second in the São Paulo regional U14 group with five games to go. The club wants the title, I want the boys to play properly. Main problem is the left side: our left-back moved up an age group and I have nobody who can overlap.

projects.name: Home kitchen renovation
projects.text: With my brother-in-law I am redoing my mother's kitchen. We pulled out the old tiles last weekend. The plumber says the floor drain is in the wrong place, so I will be hacking concrete next Saturday.

projects.name: Futsal with my daughter's team
projects.text: Coaching Bia's under-10 futsal team on Saturday mornings. Nine girls, two of whom only want to talk.

notes.text: Training: 45 minutes of rondos, the boys are sharper than last month. Gabriel, the 13-year-old number 8, took three touches when one would do. I made him stand on a cone for the next rondo. He looked at me as if I had insulted his mother.
Mom's dialysis day. Three hours in the chair, I drove her. She told the nurse I am a famous coach. I am not. The nurse smiled.

The academy's season runs March to early December. In the middle of December we break until late February. No pay in that window, the contract says so. I have always used it to take the family to my wife's parents in Santos. This year there will not be enough for even that.

Called my sister Ana about money. Mom's dialysis plus the transport plus the medicines come to about 4,200 reais a month and the insurance covers only part of it. I told her I'd take any coaching job abroad for the off-season. A camp, a clinic, anything. She laughed, then she said, are you serious.
Watching a video of a Spanish academy session. They do a 7v7 with five zones. I will try it next week and tell the boys it is my idea.
Kitchen: the plumber moved the drain. I am down 800 reais. My wife pointed out that we do not have a kitchen but we do have a receipt.
Saturday futsal: lost 6-1. Bia scored the one. She did a cartwheel. I told her we do not celebrate with cartwheels but I also took the video.
Club meeting: the director told us the contracts forbid any outside coaching work during the season, March through early December. He said it twice, looking at me. I did not say anything.
Wrote down my English phrases for a possible tryout interview: 'I build teams from the back.' 'I work with technical players.' I recorded myself. I sound like an anxious waiter.

messages.text:
Ana: How was mom today?
Me: Tired but ok. Her blood pressure was fine.
Ana: Did you ask about the new price for the sessions?
Me: Yes. It went up again.

Camila: The plumber says Saturday.
Me: Ok. I will bring the hammer.
Camila: And Bia has a game at 9.
Me: I will be there at 8:45.

Mati: Rafa, we're doing a clinic in Rosario in January. Want to come?
Me: Can't, I do not have the money for the flight.
Mati: If I hear of something with a stipend I will tell you.

Director: Rafael, remember your contract: no outside work between March and early December.
Me: I know.
Director: Good. We are counting on you for the final stretch.

relations.about: Sixty-eight, on dialysis three times a week for the past year.
Lives in Campinas, pays part of the medical costs.
Dental assistant, patient with my coaching notebooks.
Futsal fanatic, a bit of a show-off.

constraints: Cannot leave the club during the season, from March to early December
Free only from mid-December to late February
Needs a place where his family can visit or at least a stipend that covers their travel
sensitive: Mother's dialysis costs are piling up; savings are nearly gone
Embarrassed about asking friends for money
His coaching ambitions have stalled and he doubts he will ever coach a pro team
